What you will learn

  1. How to assemble a full AOI-to-provenance pipeline from reusable course helpers, without reimplementing any of them
  2. The capstone rubric you are graded against, and what satisfies each row
  3. Why the rubric weights validation design above every other criterion
Prerequisite Needed?
Module 3 (similarity + classification) Yes
Module 4 (change + validation) Yes
Module 5 (ecosystems: TESSERA/Clay/LGND) Recommended
Earth Engine account No

Time to complete: ~2 minutes execution. Runs on free Colab CPU, no Earth Engine account.

Course reference environment: 2026-08 release. Provider APIs may change. Every cloud notebook has a local/offline fallback.

Capstone rubric

Your own capstone submission (a new AOI, your own labels, your own question) is graded against these six weighted criteria. Validation design is worth more than any other single row — a convincing classifier with a dishonest validation still fails this rubric.

Criterion Weight What satisfies this row
Validation design 30% Spatial-block CV and leave-region-out (or leave-one-AOI-out), not a random split; both reported, not either/or
Reproducibility and provenance 15% course.provenance.build_provenance/write_provenance output committed alongside the notebook; pinned dataset versions
CRS and alignment correctness 15% Reprojection to a projected CRS before any metre-based operation (make_blocks, buffers); no geographic-CRS distances
Interpretation and uncertainty 15% Reported metrics carry the CV fold spread (mean ± std), not a single point estimate; claims are scoped to what was measured
Representation choice 15% The embedding product used is stated explicitly, with a one-sentence trade-off against at least one alternative
Licensing and ethics 10% Attribution and license of every input recorded; who bears the cost of a false positive is named

AOI

This is the cell a student replaces for their own capstone. The AOI knob below picks which of the course's two frozen regions this worked example runs on; a real capstone submission would point course.data.load at a newly-prepared region instead (same loader, same schema, same validation calls) — nothing downstream needs to change.

blocks.code: AOI = "bern"  # EDIT ME -- try "seville", or point course.data.load at your own AOI

import course.data
import course.schema
from course.config import ANCHOR_YEARS, AREAS

HELD_OUT_REGION = "seville" if AOI == "bern" else "bern"
assert AOI in AREAS, f"AOI={AOI!r} not in course.config.AREAS: {sorted(AREAS)}"

years = {year: course.data.load(AOI, year) for year in ANCHOR_YEARS}
held_out = course.data.load(HELD_OUT_REGION, ANCHOR_YEARS[-1])

for year, gdf in years.items():
    course.schema.validate_frozen(gdf)
course.schema.validate_frozen(held_out)
print(
    f"AOI={AOI!r}: loaded {sorted(years)} ({len(years[ANCHOR_YEARS[0]])} rows each); "
    f"held-out region {HELD_OUT_REGION!r}: {len(held_out)} rows"
)

blocks.text: AOI='bern': loaded [2018, 2021, 2024] (2050 rows each); held-out region 'seville': 2050 rows

blocks.html:
Features

Representation choice (rubric row, stated explicitly): this capstone uses AlphaEarth directly, at its native 64 dimensions. A stronger submission might compare against TESSERA or Clay per Module 5, trading off AlphaEarth's global 10 m/annual coverage against TESSERA's finer spatial resolution or Clay's Sentinel-2-derived embedding and different license terms.

The feature matrix stacks the most recent anchor year's embedding (the "current state" signal) with change_score computed between the two earlier anchor years (a "recent trend" signal) — the baseline-aware configuration PITFALLS.md's Pitfall 5 recommends: base-year embedding stacked with the delta feature, never the delta alone. A delta-only feature cannot distinguish "moved a lot from a stable state" from "moved a lot and is still moving," which is exactly the ambiguity a raw 1 - cosine threshold falls into.

blocks.code:
from course.embeddings import change_score

X_base = course.schema.to_matrix(years[ANCHOR_YEARS[-1]])
X_trend = change_score(
    course.schema.to_matrix(years[ANCHOR_YEARS[0]]),
    course.schema.to_matrix(years[ANCHOR_YEARS[1]]),
).reshape(-1, 1)
X_aoi = np.hstack([X_base, X_trend])
print(
    f"feature matrix: {X_aoi.shape} "
    f"({X_base.shape[1]} embedding dims from {ANCHOR_YEARS[-1]} + 1 change-score dim "
    f"from {ANCHOR_YEARS[0]}->{ANCHOR_YEARS[1]})"
)

blocks.text: feature matrix: (2050, 65) (64 embedding dims from 2024 + 1 change-score dim from 2018->2021)

blocks.html:
Predictions

Representation/target choice (stated explicitly, as the rubric requires): this worked example classifies the same four adequately- represented classes Module 3 used — built, crop, vegetation, water (bare dropped as a sparse residual category, per Module 3) — rather than collapsing to a binary artificialized/not-artificialized target. A capstone submission is free to pick either target; whichever is chosen, state it here and justify it, exactly as this cell does.

blocks.code:
CLASSES = ["built", "crop", "vegetation", "water"]

label_aoi = years[ANCHOR_YEARS[-1]]["label"].to_numpy()
class_mask = np.isin(label_aoi, CLASSES)
X_aoi_clf = X_aoi[class_mask]
y_aoi_clf = label_aoi[class_mask]
print(f"{AOI}: {len(y_aoi_clf)}/{len(label_aoi)} rows kept after dropping 'bare'")

from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

model = Pipeline(
    [
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("clf", LogisticRegression(random_state=RANDOM_STATE, max_iter=1000)),
    ]
)
model.fit(X_aoi_clf, y_aoi_clf)
print(f"fitted logreg on {AOI}: train accuracy={model.score(X_aoi_clf, y_aoi_clf):.3f}")

blocks.text: fitted logreg on bern: train accuracy=0.916

blocks.html:
Validation: spatial-block CV and leave-region-out

Validation design is the single largest rubric weight (30%) — larger than every other criterion combined would need to be small for that not to matter. Both validations below reuse the exact same course.validation.spatial_cv_report call shape Module 3 used, changing only groups and cv — never a hand-rolled CV loop.

blocks.code:
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold, LeaveOneGroupOut

from course.config import BLOCK_SIZE_M
from course.validation import make_blocks, spatial_cv_report

years_gdf = years[ANCHOR_YEARS[-1]].loc[class_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
epsg = AREAS[AOI]["epsg"]
gdf_projected = years_gdf.to_crs(epsg)
groups_block = make_blocks(gdf_projected, block_size_m=BLOCK_SIZE_M)
n_blocks = len(np.unique(groups_block))
assert n_blocks >= 5, (
    f"only {n_blocks} spatial blocks at block_size_m={BLOCK_SIZE_M} -- need at "
    "least 5 for GroupKFold(n_splits=5)"
)

block_report = spatial_cv_report(
    model,
    X_aoi_clf,
    y_aoi_clf,
    groups=groups_block,
    cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
)
print(
    f"SPATIAL-BLOCK CV ({AOI}, {n_blocks} blocks): balanced_accuracy="
    f"{block_report['mean_balanced_accuracy']:.3f} ± "
    f"{block_report['std_balanced_accuracy']:.3f}"
)

held_out_label = held_out["label"].to_numpy()
held_out_class_mask = np.isin(held_out_label, CLASSES)
held_out_clf = held_out.loc[held_out_class_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
X_held_out_clf = course.schema.to_matrix(held_out_clf)
# The held-out region only carries the single most-recent anchor year loaded
# above, so its feature matrix is embedding-only; pad a zero change-score
# column to match X_aoi_clf's width -- an explicit, visible substitution
# because the trend feature is undefined without a second timestamp for
# this region, not a silent shape mismatch.
X_held_out_clf = np.hstack(
    [X_held_out_clf, np.zeros((len(X_held_out_clf), 1), dtype=np.float32)]
)

X_region = np.vstack([X_aoi_clf, X_held_out_clf])
y_region = np.concatenate([y_aoi_clf, held_out_label[held_out_class_mask]])
region_groups = np.concatenate(
    [np.full(len(y_aoi_clf), AOI), np.full(len(X_held_out_clf), HELD_OUT_REGION)]
)

lro_report = spatial_cv_report(
    model, X_region, y_region, groups=region_groups, cv=LeaveOneGroupOut()
)
print(
    f"LEAVE-REGION-OUT (train {AOI}, predict {HELD_OUT_REGION}): balanced_accuracy="
    f"{lro_report['mean_balanced_accuracy']:.3f} ± "
    f"{lro_report['std_balanced_accuracy']:.3f}"
)

blocks.html: Takeaway: on this course's measured data (Module 3), leave-region-out costs roughly 17-19 balanced-accuracy points relative to in-region spatial-block CV, while spatial-block CV costs almost nothing relative to a random split. The gap printed above should show the same pattern: the honest cross-region number, not the in-region one, is where this pipeline's real generalization test lives. A capstone submission that reports only a random split, or only one of these two validations, does not satisfy the validation-design rubric row — both are required.

blocks.html:
Map: predictions over the AOI

A prediction map on its own invites a reader to treat it as settled fact. This map is deliberately paired with the uncertainty section right below it, not left as a standalone figure -- per this notebook's own rubric row on interpretation/uncertainty, and because the leave-region-out result above just showed this exact model loses a large share of its accuracy outside its training region. A ranked, human-verified candidate layer is the honest framing; an unqualified "artificialized/not" map is not.

blocks.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

pred_aoi = model.predict(X_aoi_clf)
map_gdf = years_gdf.assign(pred=pred_aoi)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
for cls, group in map_gdf.groupby("pred"):
    ax.scatter(group["lon"], group["lat"], s=8, label=cls, alpha=0.7)
ax.set_title(f"{AOI}: predicted class per point (in-region fit)")
ax.set_xlabel("lon")
ax.set_ylabel("lat")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize="small")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("figures/05_prediction_map.png")
plt.show()

blocks.html:
Uncertainty: model-level and validation-level

These are two genuinely different kinds of uncertainty, and conflating them is exactly the overconfidence trap this section exists to avoid:

  • Model uncertainty -- how close a single prediction was to a different class, for THIS fitted model on THIS data. Computed below as the margin between the top two predicted-class probabilities: a small margin means the model itself is unsure, even before asking whether the model generalizes at all.
  • Validation uncertainty -- how much the reported accuracy itself would swing under a different sample of the same evaluation, i.e. the fold-to-fold spread (std_balanced_accuracy) already computed by spatial_cv_report above. A model can show a confident (small) margin on every point and still have a large validation std -- these are not the same signal, and reporting only one is a form of the confident- map-hiding-real-uncertainty problem this phase's threat model calls out (T-05-14).

A single accuracy number, with neither of these alongside it, is an overconfident presentation of a change/classification map.

blocks.code:
proba = model.predict_proba(X_aoi_clf)
sorted_proba = np.sort(proba, axis=1)
margin = sorted_proba[:, -1] - sorted_proba[:, -2]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.hist(margin, bins=30, color="tab:blue", alpha=0.8)
ax.set_title(f"{AOI}: model-level uncertainty (top-1 minus top-2 probability margin)")
ax.set_xlabel("margin (0 = maximally uncertain, 1 = maximally confident)")
ax.set_ylabel("count")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("figures/05_uncertainty_margin_hist.png")
plt.show()

print(
    f"MODEL-LEVEL uncertainty ({AOI}): mean margin={margin.mean():.3f}, "
    f"{(margin < 0.2).sum()}/{len(margin)} points with margin < 0.2 (low confidence)"
)
print(
    f"VALIDATION-LEVEL uncertainty: spatial-block CV std_balanced_accuracy="
    f"{block_report['std_balanced_accuracy']:.3f}; leave-region-out "
    f"std_balanced_accuracy={lro_report['std_balanced_accuracy']:.3f} "
    "(fold-to-fold spread, not a per-point number)"
)

blocks.text:
MODEL-LEVEL uncertainty (bern): mean margin=0.810, 99/1900 points with margin < 0.2 (low confidence)
VALIDATION-LEVEL uncertainty: spatial-block CV std_balanced_accuracy=0.010; leave-region-out std_balanced_accuracy=0.122 (fold-to-fold spread, not a per-point number)

blocks.html: Takeaway: the map above should be read as a ranked candidate layer a human verifies -- ordered by the margin computed here, low-margin points reviewed first -- never as a finished classification. Both uncertainty numbers printed above matter: a tight model-level margin does not rescue a wide validation-level spread, and vice versa.

Provenance

Every number and figure above traces back to a specific dataset version, CRS, label source and license -- recorded once per table when it was loaded (course.data.load) and summarized here with build_provenance / write_provenance (course/provenance.py), never hand-typed. This notebook's own output is held to the same templates/PROVENANCE_CHECKLIST.md standard demonstrated throughout the course, rather than only described.

blocks.html:
Rubric self-check

The Header's rubric table, revisited here with THIS run's own evidence named for each row -- the worked example a capstone submission's own self-check should imitate:

Criterion Weight This notebook's evidence
Validation design 30% The spatial-block CV cell and the leave-region-out cell above, both required and both reported side by side in the comparison table -- not either/or
Reproducibility and provenance 15% The Provenance cell's outputs/provenance_05.json, built entirely from course.data.load's carried metadata, never hand-typed
CRS and alignment correctness 15% The gdf_projected = years_gdf.to_crs(epsg) reprojection cell before make_blocks, guarded by make_blocks' own distance-sanity assertion
Interpretation and uncertainty 15% The model-level margin histogram and the validation-level std_balanced_accuracy cells above, kept explicitly distinct
Representation choice 15% The Features section's explicit AlphaEarth-at-64-D choice, stated with its trade-off against TESSERA/Clay
Licensing and ethics 10% The Wrap-up's verbatim attribution/license strings below, plus the false-positive-cost statement: a false "artificialized" flag on someone's land can trigger real regulatory or compliance consequences, so a low-confidence flag (per the margin histogram above) must never be presented as certain. Inferred labels like "artificialized" can also be more sensitive than the underlying imagery itself -- they imply a judgment about the land's status that the raw pixels alone do not.

Wrap-up

Takeaways:

  • This capstone template assembles an AOI-to-provenance pipeline entirely from course helpers reused, unmodified, from Modules 3-5.
  • Validation design carries the largest rubric weight for a reason: the leave-region-out gap measured earlier is the single largest source of overconfidence this pipeline could produce if only in-region numbers were reported.
  • A prediction map is only honest alongside both a model-level and a validation-level uncertainty measure -- neither substitutes for the other.
  • The provenance file and the rubric self-check above are not optional extras; they are graded rubric rows, produced automatically from metadata already carried by course.data.load.

What's next: the blank templates in templates/PROVENANCE_CHECKLIST.md and templates/MODEL_DATA_CARD_TEMPLATE.md are what you fill in for your own capstone AOI -- this notebook is the worked example of applying them to a finished run, not a substitute for filling them in yourself.
